Original JSON revealed source-level structure in all thirty records, so the assessment tested exact repetition, chronology, static transfer/use operations, domain-level traffic and public channel/state/report references before rotating into six exact committed-record locator queries.
snapshot_limitations: The sanitized snapshot preserves public report links, separate event and observation times, report and decoded-source hashes, domain-level traffic summaries and bounded static operation counts. It omits submitted paths, visualization URLs, request and response bodies, headers, submitter and network-origin values, credentials, personal addresses and recovered source. A transient timeout prevented a redundant aggregate archive-body comparison after the successful primary reads; therefore this pass makes no request-body or cross-response reuse claim. Hash equality, source structure and scanner multiplicity do not authenticate autonomous participants, task meaning, downstream use or an authorization boundary.

exact_source_repeat.assessment: The two records carry the same 2,662-character submitted source five seconds apart and preserve only an unresolved nghttp2 request. This is consistent with a duplicate submission or scanner retry and contains no captured recipient action.

strongest_apparent_dependencies.assessment: The only exact source repeat is a two-record burst five seconds apart. Both records preserve the same submitted program and only unresolved nghttp2 traffic, which supports duplicate submission or retry rather than a sender-to-recipient handoff.

Eight sources serialize browser-observed Tableau metadata and assign navigation. Five archives record an example.com request: two return 404 and three have unknown status; the other three preserve only unresolved nghttp2 traffic. The sources contain no fetch, XHR, socket or response-read operation, and the archives expose no distinguishable autonomous recipient or downstream use.

Twenty-two records carry the older peer-language cue and eight carry repeated-requests. Source inspection resolves the former to Tableau APIs and page labels, while the strict task-or-peer lexical count is zero. Repeated visualization requests and one duplicate source do not establish participant identity or task exchange.

nghttp2_host_assessment.assessment: This second nghttp2 slice is another segment of the known AIHW Tableau browser-test sequence.
